# `Q-18-11` — Image Output Could Not Be Used

> A code cell's image output was malformed or could not be written, so the
> figure is missing from the page.

## What this means

When a Jupyter kernel returns a plot (a PNG, JPEG, or SVG image), Quarto
saves it as a file next to your document, in a `<document>_files/` folder,
and links it into the page.

This warning means that for one cell Quarto could not do that. Either the
image data the kernel sent could not be decoded (it was not valid base64),
or the file could not be written (for example, a file already exists where
the `<document>_files/` folder has to go, or the folder is read-only). The
message names the cell's position in your file, the image type, and the
reason.

The render continues. The page shows the text representation the kernel
sent with the image, such as `<Figure size 640x480>`. When the kernel sent
none, the page shows the placeholder \[Image output\].

## How to fix

If the reason is a write failure, fix the folder named in the message and
render again.

If the image data was malformed, the kernel is sending something Quarto
cannot read. Re-run the render to rule out a one-off failure. If it recurs,
report it with the kernel's name and version.

Use `--strict` to make this warning stop the render:

```bash
q2 render --strict
```
